angularDiameterSource: No angular diameter is measured: this is the model radius, 0.12 solar radii (Climent et al. 2022), at the Gaia distance.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 source 3526198184723289472: parallax 47.2733 mas, inverted to 21.1536 pc with no zero-point correction.
radiusSource: Radius 0.12 solar radii: the radius Climent et al. (2022, A&A 660, A65; arXiv:2201.12606) adopt for each component of the pair, from the Chabrier et al. (2000) evolutionary models at the pair's age and mass (they give 0.12 to 0.14 over those ranges); a model radius, since neither star's disc is measured. 83,484 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. GM: half the dynamical total mass 0.141 +/- 0.008 solar masses of the A-B orbit (Dupuy et al. 2023, MNRAS 519, 1688; doi:10.1093/mnras/stac3557; arXiv:2208.08448, Table 3), because Dupuy et al. find the two nearly equal (K-band flux ratio 0.033 +/- 0.004 mag; 74 +/- 4 Jupiter masses each if the mass ratio is near unity) while their fitted mass ratio, 0.45 +/- 0.08, is poorly constrained; times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 2700 K: the best-fitting BT-Settl model to the pair's combined spectrum (Dupuy et al. 2023, section 4), which describes both stars only because they are nearly equal. presentationUp: the display axis (celestial north at the star) is up; no spin axis is measured on the sky.
effectiveTemperatureSource: 2700 K: the best-fitting BT-Settl model to the pair's combined spectrum, Dupuy et al. (2023, MNRAS 519, 1688), section 4, https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.08448

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published model radius. The star's disc is not resolved; its colour is a blackbody at the published temperature.
